_doc: Already-reported upstream issues. A discrepancy matching an entry in `entries` is closed as DUPLICATE (open issue) or DESIGN_DIVERGENCE (closed as intended), with the link. Add an entry every time you file or find an issue so the campaign stops re-triaging it. Fields: kind (only_mypy|only_ty|reveal_mismatch|reveal_unpaired|concern_mismatch), silent_tool, codes (diagnostic codes of the reporting tool), message (regex on its message), statement (optional regex on the statement), source (optional regex on the whole program), dismissal, url, note, an optional demote_on_exception (true: the entry steps aside and the finding stays in review when CPython raised a type-related exception in that statement) and an optional stance (open|intended|not_planned|duplicate-of) used by the prior-stance check (typediff/priors.py). `prior_stances` entries NEVER dismiss anything: they only cap a would-be CONFIRMED/CANDIDATE finding at REVIEW and attach the stance + url to the draft. Fields: id, stance, url, note, kinds (discrepancy kinds, gate), and either a signature (message/codes/statement/source) or tags (feature tags that must all be present in the statement or program). Searching the tracker and discuss.python.org stays a manual step: check the BODY text, not only titles. CRASH entries (kind "crash", matched in typediff/crash_upstream.py from the pipeline because crash findings have no discrepancy): fields id, kind, tool (mypy|ty|pyright; one entry per tool, the same program can crash two tools with two different issues), signature (regex, re.fullmatch against the crash signature, e.g. ty:signal-SIGABRT:stack-overflow, mypy:signal-SIGSEGV, pyright:internal:RangeError, <tool>:timeout), requires (MANDATORY name in crash_upstream._CRASH_REQUIRES, a pure function of the parsed program: a crash is dismissed only when tool AND signature AND source shape all match, never on tool + signature alone), dismissal (DUPLICATE), stance, url, note. Crash entries build no KB entry and have no kb-selftest example.

entries.message: Value of type variable .* cannot be
entries.note: open ty issue: ty allows passing different types for constrained TypeVar arguments
closed as intended: Unpack[TD] of an *open* TypedDict accepts extra keywords (python/typing#2272); use closed=True for strict checking

entries.message: overrides class .* in an incompatible manner
entries.note: open ty issue: overriding a method that takes Self as a non-receiver parameter should be a Liskov violation (only pyright reports it)
Known mypy false negative: an inferred lambda retains narrowing of a captured optional parameter even after explicit reassignment to None; narrow AST matcher only. Verified on mypy 2.4.0.

HONEST STATUS: #948 is an open FEATURE REQUEST, not a statement that mypy is right; this dismissal is KNOWN_LIMITATION (a tracked, unimplemented mypy check), and ty's report is arguably correct (the code raises NameError on 3.13 without a future import). The silent tool is mypy. Issue opened and read: open mypy enhancement request, opened and read (title: 'Detect if required string literal escapes are missing from a type'; body: 'Mypy should complain about code that isn't using string literal escaped when they are required', example `def (self) -> A: ...  # Should be an error; string literal escape required`): mypy does not report a missing string-literal escape for a forward reference in an annotation, which raises NameError at runtime when annotations are evaluated eagerly (Python < 3.14 without `from __future__ import annotations`); the duplicate python/mypy#3088 was closed in its favour. Narrow AST matcher: unquoted name inside an annotation of the same statement, naming a class of the file defined later or enclosing the statement, no future import, ty and pyright agree it is undefined. Many harvested mypy .test files rely on this leniency.

open (bug, fatal, protocols; state as of 2026-11-04): ty aborts with a stack overflow on two generic protocols where P1.a takes P1[T2] and P2.a takes P1[T2] | P2[T2]; no call needed (origin: mypy check-protocols.test testTwoUncomfortablyIncompatibleProtocolsWithoutRunningInIssue9771). Verified on ty 0.0.84 (ty_TB, t20a, ty_20 reproducers).

closed as completed on 2026-11-03 (performance; fix referenced by the team as astral-sh/ruff#29933, not verified by us), and ty 0.0.84 still showed it (FIXED in ty 0.0.97, verified 2026-11-06: ty_TA_depth24 now finishes in 0.06 s with no diagnostics; the entry stays so stored runs from <= 0.0.84 still close as duplicates): comparing two values of the same deeply nested tuple alias (type Tn = tuple[T(n-1), T(n-1)], depth >= 12) takes exponential time, seen by the pipeline only as a runner timeout (depth 20 takes ~9.5 s on 0.84, depth 24 exceeds the 120 s default). Kept as a historical entry; on the pinned 0.0.97 nothing reproduces.

open (bug, fatal, paramspec; state as of 2026-11-04): stack overflow when a function generic over Callable[P, R] (ParamSpec plus a separate return TypeVar) is called with itself, id(id). Callable[[T], T], Callable[P, int] and id(g) do not crash. Verified on ty 0.0.84.

open (bug, fatal, attributes, callables, cycles; state as of 2026-11-05): ty overflows its stack when an instance is called and its class declares __call__ as an attribute annotated with the class itself (class C: __call__: 'C'; C()()), also with Self or a union holding C or Self. The issue shows the exact two-line program; a fix attempt (ruff#28691) was closed unmerged. Verified on ty 0.0.84 and 0.0.97. Same shape as MYPY-22361 (the mypy crash on the same programs). Since Day 5 the matcher (call_attr_own_type) also covers every __call__ attribute type that leads back to its class and is then called, verified on ty 0.0.84 and 0.0.97 in campaign/day4/verify-v1.md section 4: mutually recursive pairs (A.__call__: B, B.__call__: A), a three-class chain, ClassVar[...], 'B | None' pairs, subclass instances, a call through a union-typed parameter (obj: C | Other), and a local bound by c = C() and then called (Day-5 seed 0bc328316b4c; the issue program with one more line). __call__: int, an unrelated class, list[C] and a __call__ method do not crash and are not matched.

open (bug, fatal, cycles, paramspec; state as of 2026-11-04): a class whose __init__ types self as Callable[P, T] plus a __call__ typed over Callable[P, T] with one more named parameter makes ty run out of memory and abort (classmethod __call__; the pipeline sees the abort as ty:timeout or ty:signal-SIGKILL depending on host memory) or panic 'too many cycle iterations' (plain method). Needs the extra parameter and a U() call. Verified on ty 0.0.84.

open (bug, fatal, generics, cycles; state as of 2026-11-04): stack overflow when a generic class C has base N[N['C[C[X]]']] (C expanding inside its own argument) and N[C[int]] is then checked. The non-expanding base N[N['C[X]']] and a program without the N[C[..]] use do not crash. Verified on ty 0.0.84. The mypy crash on the same program is MYPY-22360, a different entry.

open (crash; state as of 2026-11-04): compiled mypy segfaults (uncompiled: RecursionError) on type X = Meta[X] with type Meta[T] = type[T], a self-reference through another generic alias. type A = A and type X = type[X] are rejected cleanly. The bare-parameter variant type Id[T] = T; type X = Id[X] hangs instead (different symptom, not matched). Verified on mypy 2.4.0.
open (crash, topic-recursive-types; state as of 2026-11-04): segfault on a class parameterised by T = TypeVar('T', default='T'). The bare TypeVar and def f(x: T) do not crash. Verified on mypy 2.4.0.

open (crash, topic-recursive-types; state as of 2026-11-04): segfault checking C against N[C] where N is contravariant and class C(N[N['C']]) refers back to C; the class definitions alone, and invariant or covariant Z, do not crash. Verified on mypy 2.4.0. The ty crash on the same program is TY-4900, a different entry.

open (crash, topic-recursive-types; state as of 2026-11-04): segfault when an instance is called and its class declares __call__ as an attribute annotated with the class itself, Self | None or C | None. The declaration alone, __get__: C and __call__: int do not crash. Verified on mypy 2.4.0. Since Day 5 the matcher also covers the other __call__ attribute types that lead back to their class (mutual pairs, chains, ClassVar, subclass instances, calls through a union-typed parameter, a local bound by c = C() and then called; campaign/day4/verify-v1.md section 4), same as TY-4148. The decorated-__get__ program (A7) also crashes mypy 2.4.0 but its relation to this issue is unconfirmed, so it is not matched.

open (bug; state as of 2026-11-04): RangeError 'Maximum call stack size exceeded' when __init__ or __new__ (or a metaclass __call__) is declared as type['C'] of its own class and the class is instantiated. Verified on pyright 1.1.414.

closed as completed on 2026-11-03 (a maintainer comment points at PR #11968), but the pinned pyright 1.1.414 still hangs (no output after 60 s) on type GrowingList[T] = list[GrowingList[T | GrowingList[T]]] once the alias is specialised in an annotation; kept as an entry because the pinned version reproduces. The declaration alone does not hang.

closed as completed on 2026-11-02, fixed by astral-sh/ruff#29903; ty 0.0.84 still reproduced it, FIXED in ty 0.0.97 (verified 2026-11-06: first(a) is now int and the bad assignment is reported; kb-selftest example no longer fires, so it is stored as example_pre_0_0_97). Kept for stored runs from <= 0.0.84. Original description (state as of 2026-11-04): ty cannot solve a TypeVar from a generic TypedDict argument (Resp[int] passed to Resp[T] leaves T Unknown), so a bad assignment of the call result is silently accepted; mypy and pyright report it. Narrow AST matcher: the statement calls a function with a parameter Resp[T] over a generic TypedDict. Verified on ty 0.0.84; not reproducible on 0.0.97.
same root cause as TY-4884 (closed 2026-11-02, fixed by astral-sh/ruff#29903; reproduced on ty 0.0.84, FIXED in ty 0.0.97): reveal_type of the call result is Unknown on ty and int on mypy/pyright.

entries.message: Type `Unknown` does not match asserted type
entries.note: same root cause as TY-4884 (closed 2026-11-02, fixed by astral-sh/ruff#29903; reproduced on ty 0.0.84, FIXED in ty 0.0.97): assert_type of the call result sees Unknown because ty could not solve the TypeVar from the generic TypedDict.

open mypy bug (state as of 2026-11-04): PEP 695 variance inference treats a writable Callable[[T], None] attribute as contravariant, so Handler[float] is accepted as Handler[int] and the later callback reassignment fails at runtime; ty and pyright infer invariant and reject. Narrow AST matcher: the class named in ty's message is PEP 695 and stores a non-Final, non-underscore Callable[[..T..], R] attribute (class annotation or self.x = param) or a public property whose @x.setter takes such a Callable (the issue body lists 'a property with a setter' as the same behaviour); Final attributes, read-only properties and plain methods are not covered. Verified on mypy 2.4.0 (Day-5 seed a660052c7821).

open mypy bug (bug, priority-0-high, topic-type-narrowing; state as of 2026-11-04): mypy keeps the narrowing of a constant-index subscript (xs[0] is not None, isinstance(t[0], int)) after an assignment to that same subscript, so later uses see the stale type and ty/pyright's diagnostic is missing. Narrow AST matcher: constant subscript narrowed, assigned, then used in the reported statement; attribute narrowing (mypy resets it), variable indices and del are not covered. Verified on mypy 2.4.0.
same root cause as MYPY-20969 (open; state as of 2026-11-04): reveal_type of the subscript after the assignment shows mypy's stale narrowed type (int) where ty and pyright show the assigned type.

open mypy bug (bug, topic-enum, topic-type-narrowing; reopened; state as of 2026-11-04): mypy narrows an enum.Flag like a plain Enum, expanding it into its members, although the typing spec exempts Flag because members combine arbitrarily. The issue shows the == form; the same root cause makes the final else of an `x is F.A / elif x is F.B` chain look unreachable, so errors there are never reported (ty and pyright report them). Narrow AST matcher: the statement is in the final else of such a chain over a Flag/IntFlag subclass; the same chain over a plain Enum is not covered. Known limit: the matcher does not check that the chain tests every member, so a partial chain could be over-matched. Verified on mypy 2.4.0.

same root cause as MYPY-21937 (open, reopened; state as of 2026-11-05): mypy expands an enum.Flag into its members, so the final else of an `x is F.A / elif x is F.B` chain over a Flag is treated as unreachable and reveal_type there prints nothing, although CPython runs that branch (a combined value such as F.A | F.B reaches it). ty and pyright reveal a type there. Narrow AST matcher: the statement is in the final else of such a chain over a Flag/IntFlag subclass. Verified on mypy 2.4.0 (Day-5 seeds 21e5664f55a9, 7517113c9957, 93344aa813c2, b3771201cb49) and in campaign/day4/verify-v2.md section 4.4.

open ty umbrella issue 'Enums: advanced features' (state as of 2026-11-05), unchecked item 'Handling of enum.Flag (enum expansion may not be performed for subclasses of enum.Flag)': ty reveals F.R | F.W as Literal[F.R, F.W] where mypy and pyright reveal F, although the runtime value <F.R|W: 3> is neither member. Narrow AST matcher: the statement uses a bitwise combination of two Flag/IntFlag members, or the inversion ~F.X of one member (ty reveals ~F.W as Literal[F.W], runtime F.R; campaign/day4/verify-v2.md section 4.4), directly or through a variable assigned from one. Verified on ty 0.0.84.

closed as completed on 2026-01-16 (PR #20492 reworked equality and identity narrowing only), but mypy 2.4.0 still reproduces the rest (state as of 2026-11-05): mypy treats an enum member that is a runtime ALIAS of an earlier member as a member of its own. The issue body says 'aliases or duplicate values' and cites the Python docs rule that a second member with the same value is an alias; a second symptom, assert_never on an alias, is the open mypy#21117 (explicit alias form). Here mypy rejects x: Literal[E.A] = E.B, assert_type(E.B, Literal[E.A]) or assert_never(e) although E.B is E.A at runtime; ty matches CPython, pyright has the same limitation (pyright#11100, open). Narrow AST matcher: a mypy message names Literal[E.alias] where alias repeats an earlier constant value of the same Enum/IntEnum/StrEnum (True after 1 included) or is assigned an earlier member; auto() values, a custom __new__ and Flag classes are not judged. Verified on mypy 2.4.0 (campaign/day4/verify-v3.md section 1, Day-5 seeds 5b98a456c114, 744e0c9a2bca, 99f2b5bbcca2, bcac6db24c36).

same root cause as MYPY-16830 (state as of 2026-11-05): reveal_type of an enum alias member (ONE = 1; UNO = 1, or TRUE = True after ONE = 1 in an IntEnum) shows the alias as a member of its own (Literal[E.UNO], .value Literal[True]) where ty shows the first member and its value (Literal[E.ONE], Literal[1]), which is what CPython does (E.UNO is E.ONE). pyright shows the alias too (pyright#11100). Narrow AST matcher: the statement reads E.alias of a value-duplicate or assigned alias.

entries.message: Type `Literal\[.*` does not match asserted type
entries.example:
import enum
from typing import assert_type


class F(enum.Flag):
    R = 1
    W = 2


v = F.R | F.W
assert_type(v, F)
entries.note: same unchecked item of the open umbrella issue ty#876 (state as of 2026-11-04): assert_type(F.R | F.W, F) is rejected by ty because it expands a Flag combination to Literal[F.R, F.W]; mypy and pyright accept it. Verified on ty 0.0.84.

entries.example:
import enum
from typing import Literal


class F(enum.Flag):
    R = 1
    W = 2


def only_r(x: Literal[F.R]) -> int:
    return 1


combined = F.R | F.W
assert combined.value == 3
only_r(combined)
entries.note: same unchecked item of the open umbrella issue ty#876 (state as of 2026-11-05), mypy-only row: ty expands the Flag combination to Literal[F.R, F.W], derives combined.value as Literal[1, 2], so `assert combined.value == 3` narrows it to Never and the later call is unreachable for ty; mypy and pyright correctly reject passing the combined Flag to a Literal[F.R] parameter. ty is silent only because of the Flag expansion. Narrow AST matcher: the mypy message names a Flag/IntFlag class of the program and the statement uses a bitwise combination of two members of it. The entry steps aside when CPython raises a type-related exception in that statement. Verified on ty 0.0.84 and 0.0.97.

entries.message: "self" parameter missing for a non-static method
entries.note: open (lint; state as of 2026-11-05, 'no error when instance method has no `self` parameter'): mypy reports [misc] on a function defined in a class body without a self parameter (and not a staticmethod), e.g. a helper used as a decorator inside the class body; pyright reports it too (reportSelfClsParameterName), ty reports nothing at the definition. A maintainer in the issue is unsure it should be a ty error (ty already rejects calling it on an instance) and suggests a ruff rule. Verified on mypy 2.4.0, pyright 1.1.414 and ty 0.0.97 (Day-6 seeds 49c0a3858dbb, 3eb405b1e819, 853fdc9fd282).

prior_stances.note: open (unsoundness, diagnostics; state as of 2026-11-05; the design is recorded in the closed ty#2140): ty folds a comparison of a tuple type to Literal[True] / Literal[False] on the assumption that tuple subclasses do not override __eq__, __ne__, __lt__ ... __len__, __bool__; the issue asks for a diagnostic on such overrides. A program that defines such a tuple (or NamedTuple) subclass and gets a Literal from ty is this issue (campaign/day4/verify-v2.md section 2). Kept as a prior stance and NOT as a dismissal: calibration/must_stay_live/ty_constant_fold_tuple_subclass.py must stay live.

reported by us, closed as intended behaviour (design divergence), not a bug (closed 'Not planned' 2026-10-05; same topic as ty#4849, closed as duplicate 2026-10-28, where carljm calls ty's behaviour intentional and more correct): ty treats Self in a method signature as a TypeVar bounded by the defining class and solves it jointly with the receiver, so Leaf().add(Node()) is accepted; mypy/pyright pin Self to the receiver. The spec is ambiguous. A crash through Self-typed state (list[Self], next: Self | None) is a different, genuine unsoundness

TypeVarTuple constraint-set implementation is already tracked. Callable[[*Ts], R] plus *args: *Ts can accept incompatible types or arity (verified ty 0.0.84/0.0.91). Related ty#4262. Treat as potentially known; this broad prior does not dismiss findings or establish an exact duplicate.

display bug (labelled bug; state checked 2026-11-05: closed as duplicate on 2026-10-05, so it is tracked elsewhere): reveal_type of a bound method prints Self/TypeVar parameters specialised to the receiver (e.g. `Leaf.add(c: Leaf)`), which is not what call checking uses

open (bug label): the earlier design discussion of the same example, including the 'reveal_type contradicts the accepted call' observation. Its body text contains the Node/Leaf add(c: Self) program, so a title search would not find it

open mypy bug (bug, topic-dataclasses, topic-runtime-semantics; state as of 2026-11-04): mypy reports attr-defined for class access of an InitVar field that has a default (Sub.extra), which CPython allows (dataclasses leaves the default as a class attribute); pyright rejects the same access, so the expected behaviour is contested. Treated as an unconfirmed design question: caps at REVIEW, never dismisses.

closed as a duplicate on 2026-06-17 (state as of 2026-11-04); the maintainer comment points at ty#876 (ty does not support enum.Flag yet). The issue itself is about `int() & Flags.A` narrowed to Literal[Flags.A] for an IntFlag, a related but different operand than a Flag|Flag combination. Related prior only: caps at REVIEW, never dismisses.
